reason: The agent adds per-marker feedback to mod_assign_get_submission_status, with marker id (anonymised to -1 when the grader is hidden), plugin editor fields and files from the marker file areas scoped by mark id. That is what the issue asks for. The hidden externallib test fails at assertTrue(isset($result['feedback']['markerfeedback'])) because the agent named the field 'markersfeedback' and has no 'position'/'workflowstate' subfields. The locallib test fails because it expects comments get_file_areas() to also return 'feedback_marker', while the agent put marker areas in a new get_marker_file_areas() method. Both are API and naming choices the issue does not specify.

The agent's change to core\check\table is functionally identical to the human fix: it builds details from all results instead of only failing ones. The hidden check_table_test.php errors in setUpBeforeClass because it requires tests/fixtures/check/fixture_check.php. The developers added that fixture class and it was not copied over, so the failure comes from a missing human-added fixture, not from the agent's code.

The issue concerns 'OAuth 2 clients', which is the UI term for clients of Moodle's OAuth2 server (core\oauth2\server\client_manager). The developers added config-log entries there for create/update/disable/reactivate/delete, redirect URIs and secrets. The agent instead added logging to core\oauth2\api (issuers, endpoints, user field mappings) and left client_manager untouched. The tests' config_log entries for 'oauth2serverclient' are never written, so the change is in the wrong subsystem.

The agent returns false from linearnavigationsettings::show_navigation_footer whenever $page->cm->is_stealth(), which hides the footer for every user. The hidden test cases 'Admin: Stealth module' and 'Admin: Section hidden, visible module' expect true for an admin because the developers exempt users with moodle/course:viewhiddenactivities. The issue says the footer should be hidden 'when a user is viewing a stealth activity' and never mentions a capability exemption, so the agent's reading is reasonable but differs from the developers' choice.

Both patches always add the CORS headers, which fixes the problem the issue raises. They differ on Content-Type: the agent forces application/json/inline unless HTML is explicitly accepted (so also for no Accept header and for */*), while the developers force it only when application/json is explicitly accepted or for OPTIONS/HEAD. The hidden tests test_cors_headers_added_for_non_json_request and test_cors_headers_added_for_wildcard_accept_request assert Content-Type is '' and fail. The issue only discusses CORS headers and leaves the Content-Type policy for wildcard requests open.

The agent changed the query to COUNT(DISTINCT u.id), which counts users with attempts rather than attempts. The human fix uses COUNT(DISTINCT ha.id). With two users and 1+2 attempts, test_count_attempts_with_multiple_enrolments expects 6 and the existing count_attempts tests also fail (6 failures). The method no longer returns the number of attempts, so the patch is wrong whatever the tests check.
